papers.title: A Topology-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Multi-Target Active Debris Removal using Gaussian Boson Sampling
papers.abstract: The continued growth of orbital debris threatens the safety and sustainability of near-Earth space, making Active Debris Removal (ADR) an important mitigation strategy. Selecting $k$ targets from $N$ candidates yields a combinatorial search space of size $\binom{N}{k}$, making joint target selection and mission sequencing computationally demanding. We present a topology-aware quantum-classical framework integrating orbital mechanics, weighted orbital-transfer graphs, Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS), and multi-objective evolutionary optimization. Seven target-prioritization strategies represent physical consequence, orbital persistence, conjunction risk, network centrality, community structure, inferred source families, and random selection. GBS generates candidate target subsets from the weighted graph, which are then evaluated using PyGMO-based evolutionary optimization to identify servicing sequences that jointly minimize total velocity increment ($\Delta v$) and mission duration, accounting for modeled timing, propulsion, and mass feasibility. We evaluate the framework across three benchmark environments, SOCRATES Minefield, Collision Cloud, and Random, with candidate-pool sizes $N\in\{15,18,22,25\}$ and target cardinalities $k\in\{3,5\}$. The experiments characterize how benchmark topology, prioritization strategy, and problem scale relate to sampling behavior and downstream mission performance. By separating candidate-subset generation from detailed trajectory optimization, the framework offers a topology-aware approach to focusing computational effort on a limited set of candidate ADR missions.

papers.title: Real-to-Sim Calibration of Bosch Etching Simulators with Few-Shot XSEM Data and Hybrid Search
papers.abstract: The Bosch process is widely used in MEMS and TSV fabrication, but accurate prediction of etching outcomes remains difficult without calibration against real measurements, which are sparse and costly to obtain. This work presents a few-shot real-to-sim calibration framework that decouples simulator parameters from direct process variables to infer a recipe-specific simulator parameter vector from sparse measurements, enabling reliable prediction of etch depth and sidewall angle under held-out process conditions. We first formulate Bosch profile prediction as a few-shot real-to-sim calibration problem, where a small set of real XSEM measurements is used to identify a recipe-specific ViennaPS parameter vector $z_r^*$ that minimizes the discrepancy between simulated and measured etch depth and sidewall angle. To search this parameter space efficiently, the framework combines local exploration, LLM-guided candidate generation, and XGBoost-based surrogate screening, while retaining ViennaPS simulation as the final verification step for each selected candidate. Experiments on two Bosch etching recipes show that the proposed framework accurately predicts held-out etching results, achieving normalized global errors of 0.340 and 0.249 for the 2 recipes respectively.

papers.title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization for Targeted Structural Dynamic Vibration Attenuation
papers.abstract: Resonance-induced excessive vibrations can degrade performance, reduce reliability, and shorten the service life of engineering structures. To reduce the risk of resonance, structural natural frequencies are generally engineered to be shifted away from excitation frequencies. To achieve these frequency shifts, topology optimization provides a systematic approach to tailor structural stiffness and mass as an effective inverse design approach. Multi-material topology optimization exploits the high-dimensional design space of spatially varying material constituents by simultaneously optimizing material selection and spatial distribution over the design domain, offering great flexibility in controlling natural frequencies. This study proposes a multi-material topology optimization that attenuates excessive structural dynamic vibrations in free-vibration scenarios via a novel multivariate weight-based interpolation method. Additionally, to address non-smoothness due to mode switching amid optimization, we employ a bound formulation with an auxiliary scalar design variable to replace the max-min eigenvalue objective with constraints on individual eigenvalues. Furthermore, we study and compare three optimization formulations for multi-material design to attenuate vibrations, including maximizing fundamental eigenfrequency, maximizing the gap between adjacent eigenfrequencies, and excluding frequencies from targeted frequency bands, which are smoothly approximated by a proposed rational polynomial formulation. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of our proposed method.

papers.title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Phononic Crystals for Targeted Elastic Wave Bandgap
papers.abstract: Phononic crystals are periodic elastic structures that exhibit frequency bandgaps within which elastic waves cannot propagate. The formation and width of these bandgaps depend on the spatial distribution of material properties within periodic phononic unit cells. In this work, we propose novel topology optimization formulations to achieve multi-material design of phononic crystals for bandgap optimization at targeted frequencies, where we discover the influence of spatially varying properties of base materials on the band structures that block and permit elastic wave propagation. Specifically, we model wave propagation by Floquet-Bloch theory and solve the resulting eigenvalue problem by the finite element method along the boundary of the irreducible Brillouin zone. We first propose a multivariate weight-based method via a novel interpolation scheme that maps the design variables of an arbitrary number of candidate materials into effective density and stiffness for elastic wave-propagation calculations, where bandgaps arise from the contrast in the stiffness and inertia among material constituents. We then develop two formulations for bandgap optimization. The first formulation maximizes the gap between two adjacent frequency bands using a bound-based approach, where we introduce two auxiliary scalar variables as additional design variables and incorporate them directly into the design objective, yielding a linear, differentiable design objective, with the eigenfrequencies entering the formulation through associated constraints. The second formulation places a bandgap over a user-defined target frequency range through a dynamic band-pairing strategy, where we adaptively identify the relevant pair of adjacent bands amid optimization iterations. Towards the end, we validate the bandgap performance of our designs against the transmission loss spectra computed from COMSOL Multiphysics.

papers.title: Freeform Programmable Liquid Crystal Elastomers via Monolithic Integration of Co-Optimization and 4D-Printing
papers.abstract: Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are active materials capable of large, reversible thermally induced actuation, offering significant potential for applications such as artificial muscles and soft robotics. However, their broader deployment is hindered by the lack of a unified design-to-fabrication framework, the strong coupling among geometry, director fields, and manufacturing constraints, and the difficulty of reliably translating complex designs into physically realizable architectures. Here, we present an autonomous and monolithic integration of co-optimization and 4D printing that enables the end-to-end design-to-realization of versatile programmable LCE architectures with superior precision, complexity, and versatility. The proposed framework establishes a unified design strategy that co-optimizes the freeform multilayer geometry and fully continuous layer-specific director distributions, and subsequently translates the optimized fields into fabrication-ready DIW toolpaths through an automated manufacturing-aware pipeline. To bridge computation and realization, we develop an optimization-centered 4D printing approach with automated, fabrication-aware toolpath generation tailored for direct ink writing of LCEs. With the proposed design-to-fabrication paradigm, we experimentally realize architectures that exhibit complex, non-intuitive thermo-mechanical behaviors. Experiments achieve highly challenging prescribed functionalities beyond the reach of intuition-based approaches and show excellent agreement with numerical simulations across all samples. This work establishes a generalizable inverse design and physical realization of freeform programmable LCE systems, enabling function-oriented and optimization-driven intelligent LCE applications for next-generation soft robotic and responsive material engineering.

papers.title: A Highly Efficient Depth-Averaged Material Point Method for Geophysical Mass Flows
papers.abstract: Probabilistic hazard assessment of geophysical mass flows requires large simulation ensembles and thus fast and robust numerical models. We present an open-source depth-averaged material point method formulated in global Cartesian coordinates, using Lagrangian particles to track the flow margin. A separate basal friction step based on the Coulomb, Voellmy, or $\mu(I)$-rheology brings the flow to rest without artificial stopping criteria. Our model reproduces analytical solutions for a sliding block and dam-break problems and matches the deposit of a laboratory granular column collapse. A back-calculation of the 2023 Brienz/Brinzauls rockslide (Switzerland) at 1m resolution (190'000 particles) runs faster than real time on a single CPU core. Calibrated to the observed runout, the three friction laws yield very similar results, but Coulomb friction shows a slightly wider affected area than Voellmy and $\mu(I)$. A probabilistic 1632-simulation ensemble at 5m resolution was computed in 76s. The model is one to two orders of magnitude faster than established depth-averaged models used in engineering practice, making catchment-style ensemble simulations feasible on a desktop computer.

papers.title: Universal neural network approximation of symmetric polyconvex energies and envelopes
papers.abstract: Symmetric polyconvexity provides a sufficient condition for weak lower semicontinuity in small-strain elasticity and a tractable lower bound for the relaxation of non-(quasi)convex energies. Since classical algorithms for computing such functions can be computationally expensive, neural network approximations have recently emerged as an alternative. A central difficulty with establishing such neural network based approaches for symmetric polyconvexity is the additional monotonicity property. As we show, the corresponding weight restrictions on ReLU-based input-convex networks do not yield universal approximation of the lifted representers. Here, we introduce symmetric polyconvex neural networks (SPCNNs) for constitutive modeling and approximation of symmetric polyconvex envelopes. The deep architecture combines convexity with the monotonicity required of a representer in the space of minors. We prove a universal approximation theorem for symmetric polyconvex energies, without requiring isotropy, and quantify the number of affine pieces attainable by the lifted network and derive reduced architectures for isotropic energies. Numerical examples illustrate stress-based regression and approximation of the symmetric polyconvex envelope of a double-well potential. Symmetric polyconvexity is guaranteed by construction, while the accuracy of the fitted energies and envelopes is assessed numerically.

papers.title: BeforeIT.jl: High-Performance Agent-Based Macroeconomics Made Easy
papers.abstract: BeforeIT is an open-source software for building and simulating state-of-the-art macroeconomic agent-based models (macro ABMs) based on the recently introduced macro ABM developed in [1] and here referred to as the base model. Written in Julia, it combines extraordinary computational efficiency with user-friendliness and extensibility. We present the main structure of the software, demonstrate its ease of use with illustrative examples, and benchmark its performance. Our benchmarks demonstrate that the base model built with BeforeIT is orders of magnitude faster than its original Matlab implementation, while achieving performance comparable to a highly optimised HPC implementation. Furthermore, we show how BeforeIT supports an easy construction of model variants such as the 'CANVAS' model of [2], how these variants can be evaluated at scale via an automated multicountry forecasting pipeline, and how the entire simulation can be automatically differentiated. BeforeIT is designed to facilitate reproducibility, extensibility, and experimentation. As the first open-source, industry-grade software to build macro ABMs, BeforeIT can significantly foster collaboration and innovation in the field of agent-based macroeconomic modelling. The package, along with its documentation, is freely available at https://github.com/bancaditalia/BeforeIT.jl under the Apache 2.0 license.

papers.title: An Eco-Friendly Tourism Trip Planner Driven by Z-Number Uncertainty: Evidence from Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul
papers.abstract: Deployed tourism trip planners ingest travel times and ratings as exact numbers, although routing services return travel times that vary with the hour of departure and a platform rating may rest on a handful of reviews or on hundreds of thousands. We present an eco-friendly trip planner that represents both quantities as Z-numbers, which pair a fuzzy restriction on a value with a fuzzy reliability on the evidence behind it, and that constructs them directly from routing-service observations at six departure hours and from platform review counts rather than from linguistic elicitation. A hybrid loss combines score, carbon, travel-time, and reliability terms, and an adaptive large neighborhood search returns single-day itineraries through a conversational front end. We compare the planner with a crisp-mean baseline under an identical optimizer in Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul, with fifteen points of interest and thirty seeds per city, and we evaluate the selected itineraries on their trip carbon and their total travel time. Pooled over 150 seed-paired runs, the planner lowers trip carbon from 3.24 to 2.61 kg (19.3%, Wilcoxon p = 0.017; city-clustered bootstrap interval 6.4% to 26.7%) and travel time from 123 to 109 minutes per trip (11.5%, p = 2.8e-10; interval 5.0% to 18.2%). The travel-time reductions survive a Holm correction in Baku, Istanbul, and Abu Dhabi; the carbon reduction is significant in Baku and large but uncertain in the dispersed catalogs of Dubai and Abu Dhabi; and neither metric changes in Tashkent. Review counts are estimates of at least 3,000 for every point of interest, so rating reliability does not vary, and with a single baseline, the results establish feasibility and direction rather than a general advantage. Code, routing caches, frozen routing tables, and per-seed results are openly released.

papers.title: Visibility-Graph-Based Relative Strength Indicator for Financial Market Decision-Making
papers.abstract: This study introduces the Visibility-Graph-Based Relative Strength Index (VGRSI), a causal indicator that selects and implicitly weights price increments using backward natural visibility. Independent parameters specify the aggregation window and the backward visibility range. Two aggregation variants use the magnitudes and counts of positive and negative contributions to produce values on a 0--100 scale. The VGRSI was tested in an automated walk-forward experiment based on 30-day optimisation windows followed by {7-day walk-forward windows}. This study covered DJI30, EUR/USD, and XAU/USD over 503 trading days in 2024--2025. {The VGRSI strategy produced positive cumulative net profits for all three instruments, whereas the tested classical-RSI strategy and the VGRSI variant without visibility selection produced cumulative losses under the same walk-forward procedure and trading conditions. Because the analysis covered only three instruments and one historical period, the results should be treated as preliminary.

papers.title: Noise-Robust Financial Numerical Entity Attribute Tagging
papers.abstract: Financial Numerical Entity (FNE) understanding aims to recover the meaning of numerical mentions in financial reports. Existing studies focus on concept name prediction and face two important limitations. First, labels derived from inline XBRL may contain errors because filings are usually prepared manually. Second, other important FNE attributes, such as reporting-time relation, measurement scale, and accounting sign, are less emphasized. We propose NOise-Robust Tagging for Rich Financial Numerical Entity Attributes (NORA) to address these gaps. NORA uses task-aware instance-specific weighting to attenuate the influence of noisy labels during training, and we develop an evaluation protocol that filters noisy labels in real-world test sets. In addition, we construct a large-scale benchmark containing 11.4 million FNEs in 6.3 million sentences with multi-attribute labels and filing metadata. Experiments show that NORA performs strongly compared with previous financial numeric tagging models and noisy-label baselines. Under both unfiltered and noise-filtered test settings, it achieves the best mean Accuracy and Macro F1 over the four attributes, with the largest gain on time-relation prediction, while remaining competitive on concept name, scale, and sign. These results demonstrate the value of modeling rich FNE attributes with document context while accounting for label noise in real-world financial filings.

papers.title: Forecasting Global Equity Volatility: Econometric Anchoring and Cross-Market Attention
papers.abstract: International volatility forecasting requires models to combine persistent local dynamics with information observed across different trading calendars. We propose PGA-Trans-HAR, an attention model that learns a bounded correction to a frozen heterogeneous autoregressive (HAR) forecast. A rolling predictive-connectedness graph guides spatial attention, while source masks accommodate market closures on the union calendar. We evaluate daily range-based volatility for eight equity indices from March 2013 to September 2026 at leads of 1, 5, and 22 union-calendar dates. Among seven primary forecasting models, PGA-Trans-HAR achieves the lowest equal-market average MSE at the 1- and 22-date leads and the lowest average QLIKE at all three leads. Its MSE reductions relative to HAR are 1.70% and 1.13% at the two endpoints. At the 1-date lead, the standard deviation of MSE across five fitted seeds is 0.00057, compared with 0.01260 for DCRNN-HAR and 0.03727 for GNN-HAR. The model is retained in 47 of 48 market-horizon MSE cells in the 90% Model Confidence Sets across two evaluation panels. Under historical-tail calibration, joint VaR/ES scores improve on HAR at the 1- and 5-date leads. A common intraday exposure rule yields annual CER gains of 7.89 to 9.28 basis points relative to HAR across the specified cost scenarios. These results support bounded correction of a local econometric forecast as a design for accurate and stable cross-market volatility prediction.

papers.title: Temperature-Dependent Multiphysics Modeling of Additive Friction Stir Deposition Using Multi-Task Coupled Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) involves coupled thermal and material-flow fields governed by frictional heating, plastic deformation, and tool-imposed boundary conditions. High-fidelity finite-volume methods (FVMs) can resolve these fields but are computationally expensive, while constant-property approximations can distort the predicted thermo-mechanical response. This work develops a steady-state multi-task coupled physics-informed neural network (MCoPINN) to predict three-dimensional temperature and material-flow fields while reconstructing temperature-dependent thermal conductivity, density, and specific heat from sparse property measurements. A theoretical analysis decomposes prediction error into property reconstruction and neural field-solver contributions and characterizes the discrepancy associated with constant-property models. A controlled one-dimensional nonlinear-conduction study evaluates property reconstruction under sparse measurements. The framework is then evaluated for AFSD against a temperature-dependent FVM benchmark and experimental thermocouple measurements. MCoPINN reproduces the reference thermal and material-flow fields and reduces average temperature root-mean-square error from 50.13 K for the constant-property CoPINN to 30.28 K across four traverse speeds. MCoPINN requires approximately 8.5 hours of training per condition, compared with 52 hours for the FVM benchmark. These results demonstrate computationally efficient, physics-coupled prediction with temperature-dependent material properties.

papers.title: Revisiting Structure-Based Filtering for AI-Designed Antibodies: Opportunities, Limits, and What Matters
papers.abstract: AI antibody design can generate far more candidates than can be experimentally tested, making post-generation filtering a central bottleneck. We study whether structure-prediction outputs can help prioritize AI-designed antibodies for experimental validation. We evaluate this problem on 4,184 experimentally characterized antibody-antigen pairs, combining newly generated wet-lab measurements with curated affinity data across diverse antigens and assay settings. We introduce two complementary filtering signals: Regional Interaction Contrast (RIC), which captures support for the predicted antibody-antigen interface, and Non-CDR Antibody Confidence (NAC), which measures antibody confidence outside the CDRs. Across AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, and ESMFold2, we find a striking difference in what information matters for filtering. Interface evidence is strongest when comparing candidates designed for different antigens, whereas antibody-level reliability is substantially more informative for ranking candidates within the same antigen. In particular, non-CDR antibody confidence consistently outperforms whole-antibody confidence across predictors, revealing an unexpected source of filtering signal beyond the predicted interface. Finally, we examine the information encoded in the predictor outputs themselves. Predicted structures contain substantial but incomplete binding-related signal, revealing both the opportunities and limits of structure-based filtering: better metrics can exploit current predictors more effectively, but their performance ultimately remains constrained by what those predictors can distinguish.

papers.title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
papers.abstract: Greedy State Boundary Search (GSBS) identifies transitions between relatively stable neural activity patterns in continuous recordings. Repeated template reconstruction and correlation evaluation make analyses across recordings and parameter settings computationally expensive. We present HP-GSBS, an open-source implementation that expresses the matching objective as additive interval contributions and computes t-distance from reusable correlation statistics. Streaming candidate reduction, sequential local refinement, and active-block reuse complement CPU, PyTorch CUDA, and Triton execution paths. Across seven controlled workloads with two input realizations each, median same-input speedups range from 154 to 1,730. All 168 optimized executions reproduce complete reference boundary histories and selected state counts, with a maximum absolute t-distance difference of $1.88\times10^{-11}$. Four publicly supplied BBBD EEG analysis matrices provide complementary cross-backend validation. A naturalistic fMRI application segments 4,230 angular-gyrus voxels in a group response and 16 participants; the 17 CPU fits total 213.10 seconds. Mean pairwise boundary alignment exceeds a circular-shift baseline, illustrating cohort-level use of the saved segmentations. Versioned results, recording-level parallelism, and optional low-memory execution support varied analysis scales. HP-GSBS connects an explicit mathematical reformulation of repeated computation to efficient and reproducible neural-state analysis.
